{{Short description|English chemist and academic (born 1947)}}
{{EngvarB|date=November 2017}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2017}}
'''Sir Leslie Colin Ebdon''' [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] [[Deputy Lieutenant|DL]] (born 26 January 1947 in [[Edmonton, London|Edmonton]], London) is the former Vice-Chancellor of the [[University of Bedfordshire]] and Director of Fair Access to Higher Education (head of the [[OFFA|Office for Fair Access]]).

==Education==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=January 2023}}
Ebdon attended Hemel Hempstead Grammar School (became [[The Hemel Hempstead School]] in 1970). Ebdon went on to obtain both his [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in [[Chemistry]] in 1968 and PhD in 1971 at [[Imperial College London]].

==Career==
{{BLP sources section|date=January 2023}}

===Early appointments===
After lecturing at [[Makerere University]], [[Kampala]] from 1971–3 and [[Sheffield City Polytechnic]] from 1973 to 1980, he joined what is now the [[University of Plymouth]] in 1981 as a lecturer in Analytical Chemistry. In 1989 he was promoted to Head of Department of Environmental Sciences and eventually rose to Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic Development).

Ebdon's research interests are in environmental analytical chemistry and his various contributions to our understanding of the behaviour and importance of trace elements in the environment have led to over 250 publications and to several awards.

=== Vice-Chancellor and Chief executive ===
Ebdon was appointed Vice-Chancellor and Chief executive of the University of Luton in September 2003. With the merger of the University and the Bedford campus of [[De Montfort University]] in August 2006 he became the Vice-Chancellor of the new [[University of Bedfordshire]]. He was succeeded by [[Bill Rammell]] as Vice-Chancellor on 1 September 2012, completing his move to the position of Director of Fair Access to Higher Education.<ref name=VCRammell>{{cite web|title=New Vice Chancellor starts at Bedfordshire|url=http://www.beds.ac.uk/news/2012/august/new-vice-chancellor-starts-at-bedfordshire|publisher=University of Bedfordshire|date=31 August 2012|accessdate=6 September 2012}}</ref>

===Director of Fair Access to Higher Education===
On 20 February 2012 Ebdon was appointed as Director of Fair Access to Higher Education, the regulator of fair access to higher education in England,<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Les Ebdon appointed next Director of Fair Access to Higher Education|url=https://www.offa.org.uk/press-releases/professor-les-ebdon-appointed-director-of-fair-access-to-higher-education/|publisher = Office for Fair Access|date=10 February 2012|accessdate=18 January 2016}}</ref> despite media criticism<ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/education/universityeducation/9074406/Theres-no-place-for-dreamingspires-in-Professor-Les-Ebdons-world.html|title= There's no place for dreaming spires in Professor Les Ebdon's world 
|work = The Telegraph|date=10 February 2012|accessdate=23 February 2012}}</ref> and his selection being rejected by the Commons Select Committee tasked with reviewing the recommendation.<ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/education-16946484|title= Vince Cable in stand off with MPs over Offa boss|work = BBC News|date=8 February 2012|accessdate=23 February 2012}}</ref> The Director of Fair Access was a statutory appointment by the [[Secretary of State for Business, Innovation and Skills]], and was supported by the [[OFFA|Office for Fair Access]].

=== million+ think tank ===
In August 2009, Ebdon, via the [[think tank]] '[[million+]]', made the controversial suggestion that universities broaden the social mix of their students by allowing grade boost to poorer students in a bid to increase social mobility.<ref>
{{cite web
|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/education/8192234.stm 
|title= Poorer student grade plan backed 
|work = BBC News
|date=9 August 2009  
|accessdate=23 February 2012}}</ref>

===Other appointments===
Ebdon is a member of the DTI's Measurement Advisory committee and Chair of a Sub Committee, and he is also a member of the European Union DGXII Certification Working Group, known particularly for his expertise on environmental certified reference materials.

Ebdon is a member of the Advisory Board of the Central Science Laboratory of [[Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs|DEFRA]]. He is currently Chair of Chemistry World Editorial Board and a Member of the Publications Board of the Royal Society of Chemistry.

Ebdon is a member of the Structure and Bonding College of the [[EPSRC]] and has chaired various EPSRC committees and served on many Royal Society of Chemistry, National Environmental Research Committees, Ministry of Agriculture Fisheries and Food and DTI Review Groups.

==Recognition==
Ebdon was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the 2009 New Year Honours. He was knighted in the [[2018 Birthday Honours]] in recognition of services to higher education and social mobility.<ref>[https://www.spurgeons.ac.uk/les-ebdon/ Sir Leslie Ebdon profile], spurgeons.ac.uk. Accessed 9 January 2023.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-06-08 |title=Queen’s Birthday Honours 2018: knighthood for Les Ebdon |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/queens-birthday-honours-2018-knighthood-les-ebdon |access-date=2023-04-15 |website=Times Higher Education (THE) |language=en}}</ref>

Ebdon was named one of Britain's 500 Most Influential People by [[Debrett's]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Debrett's 500: Prof Les Ebdon, CBE|url=http://www.debretts.com/people/debretts-500/education/prof-les-ebdon-cbe|website=Debrett's|publisher=Debrett's|accessdate=18 January 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150201043935/http://www.debretts.com/people/debretts-500/education/prof-les-ebdon-cbe|archivedate=1 February 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

In 1995, the American Microchemical Society awarded him the Benedetti-Pichler medal for outstanding contributions to microchemistry.<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.microchem.org/Nom2011.html#Past 
|title= Past Recipients of the A.A. Benedetti-Pichler Award 
|publisher = American Microchemical Society 
|accessdate=23 February 2012}}</ref>

In 1986, Ebdon was the Royal Society of Chemistry, Analytical division, School's Lecturer and later in that same year was awarded the 13th SAC Silver Medal<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/Archive/SACSilver/index.asp 
|title= SAC Silver Medal 
|publisher = Royal Society of Chemistry 
|accessdate=23 February 2012}}</ref> by the Royal Society of Chemistry.
